title.zh: 卷十四 列傳第八: 衡陽獻王昌 南康愍王曇朗
title.raw: 卷十四 列傳第八: 衡陽獻王昌 南康愍王曇朗 Volume 14: Chen Chang; Chen Tanlang

sentences.zh: 陳書卷十四

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 14
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 14

sentences.zh: 列傳第八

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Eight
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Eight

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王昌 南康愍王曇朗 子方泰 方慶

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chen Chang; Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang; sons Fangtai and Fangqing
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chen Chang; Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang; sons Fangtai and Fangqing

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王昌

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chen Chang
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chen Chang

sentences.zh: 衡陽獻王昌字敬業，高祖第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chen Chang, courtesy name Jingye, was the Founder's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chang, Prince Xian of Hengyang, styled Jingye, was the Founder's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 梁太清末，高祖南征李賁，命昌與宣后隨沈恪還吳興。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiping era, the Founder campaigned south against Li Bin and ordered Chang and Lady Xuan to return to Wuxing with Shen Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Liang's Taiping era, the Founder marched south against Li Bin and sent Chang and Lady Xuan back to Wuxing with Shen Ke.

sentences.zh: 及高祖東討侯景，昌與宣后、世祖並為景所囚。

translations.literal: When the Founder marched east against Hou Jing, Chang, Lady Xuan, and Emperor Wen were all imprisoned by Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder turned east against Hou Jing, Chang, Lady Xuan, and Emperor Wen were all taken prisoner by Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，拜長城國世子、吳興太守，時年十六。

translations.literal: When Jing was suppressed, Chang was appointed Heir of the Princedom of Changcheng and Administrator of Wuxing, aged sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing's defeat he was made heir of the princedom of Changcheng and administrator of Wuxing, at age sixteen.

sentences.zh: 昌容貌偉麗，神情秀朗，雅性聰辯，明習政事。

translations.literal: Chang's appearance was grand and handsome, his bearing bright and open; by nature he was clever and eloquent and well versed in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was tall and handsome, with a clear, spirited face; he was quick-witted and articulate and knew government affairs well.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣陳郡謝哲、濟陽蔡景歷輔昌為郡，又遣吳郡杜之偉授昌以經書。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Xie Zhe of Chen commandery and Cai Jingli of Jiyang to assist Chang in the commandery, and Du Zhiwei of Wu commandery to instruct him in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Xie Zhe of Chen and Cai Jingli of Jiyang to help him govern the commandery, and Du Zhiwei of Wu to teach him the classics.

sentences.zh: 昌讀書一覽便誦，明於義理，剖析如流。

translations.literal: Chang read a text once and could recite it; he understood principles clearly and reasoned with fluent penetration.
translations.idiomatic: He could read a passage once and recite it from memory, grasp doctrine clearly, and argue through a point without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 尋與高宗俱往荊州，梁元帝除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he went to Jingzhou with Emperor Xuan; Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him External Regular Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to Jingzhou with Emperor Xuan; Emperor Yuan of Liang made him external regular attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，又與高宗俱遷關右，西魏以高祖故，甚禮之。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell, he again moved with Emperor Xuan to the region west of the Pass; Western Wei treated him with great honor on the Founder's account.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell he was moved with Emperor Xuan to the northwest; Western Wei honored him greatly for the Founder's sake.

sentences.zh: 臣聞宗子維城，隆周之懋軌，封建藩屏，有漢之弘規，是以卜世斯永，寔資邢、衛，[1]鼎命靈長，實賴河、楚。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that imperial sons shore up the realm—the glorious standard of elevated Zhou—and that enfeoffed domains as screens was Han's grand rule; thus the dynasty's endurance truly relied on Xing and Wei, [1] and the sacred mandate's longevity truly depended on the lands of the He and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that kinsmen of the royal house buttress the state, as in glorious Zhou, and that enfeoffing princes to guard the borders was Han's great design; lasting rule truly drew on domains such as Xing and Wei, [1] and the mandate's endurance truly rested on great regions such as the He River lands and Chu.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下神猷光大，聖德欽明，道高日月，德侔造化。

translations.literal: We bow that Your Majesty's divine counsel shines broad, sacred virtue revered and bright, the Way towers above sun and moon, and virtue matches creation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's divine plan shines far; your sacred virtue is revered and clear; your Way rises above sun and moon; your virtue equals heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 往者王業惟始，天步方艱，參奉權謨，匡合義烈，威略外舉，神武內定，故以再康禹跡，大庇生民者矣。

translations.literal: In the past, when the royal enterprise had only begun and Heaven's course was still hard, you took part in counsel and joined righteous heroes; your martial prestige was shown abroad and divine might settled within—thus you twice restored Yu's traces and greatly sheltered the living people.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was first being won and the realm was still in peril, you shared in strategy and rallied men of honor; your power reached beyond the borders and your strength secured the court—so you twice restored the ancient order and sheltered the people.

sentences.zh: 及聖武升遐，王師遠次，皇嗣敻隔，繼業靡歸，宗祧危殆，綴旒非喻。

translations.literal: When the Sage Martial ascended far away, the royal army halted in the distance; the imperial heir was cut off afar and succession had no home; the ancestral temple was in peril and the jade beads hung loose beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage martial emperor passed away, the royal army was far away; the heir was cut off and the succession unsettled; the ancestral temple trembled and the throne seemed all but lost.

sentences.zh: 既而傳車言反，公卿定策，纂我洪基，光昭景運，民心有奉，園寢克寧，后來其蘇，復在茲日，物情天意，皎然可求。

translations.literal: Then the relay carriage announced return, the ministers fixed the plan, you took our great foundation, and the bright fortune shone forth; the people's hearts had a lord, the imperial tombs were secure, and renewal came on this day—human feeling and Heaven's intent were plainly to be sought.
translations.idiomatic: Then word came that the heir was returning, the ministers settled the succession, you took up the great foundation, and the bright age began; the people had a ruler, the tombs were safe, and renewal came on that day—men's hearts and Heaven's will alike were clear.

sentences.zh: 王琳逆命，逋誅歲久，今者連結犬羊，乘流縱釁，舟旗野陣，綿江蔽陸，兵疲民弊，杼軸用空，中外騷然，蕃籬罔固。

translations.literal: Wang Lin defied the mandate and long evaded punishment; now he has joined with dogs and sheep, riding the current to loose calamity—boats and banners in wild array, the river covered and the land hidden; troops weary and the people spent, the loom shuttles empty; within and without in turmoil, the frontier screens had no hold.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin had long rebelled and escaped justice; now he joined with barbarian allies and struck along the rivers—fleets and banners filled the land, the Yangzi hidden and the shores covered; armies were exhausted, the people drained, and the realm was in uproar while the borders gave way.

sentences.zh: 乃旰食當朝，憑流授律，蒼兕既馳，長蛇自翦，廓清四表，澄滌八紘，雄圖遐舉，仁聲遠暢，德化所覃，風行草偃，故以功深於微禹，道大於惟堯，豈直社稷用寧，斯乃黔黎是賴。

translations.literal: You then ate late at court and issued orders upon the current; the azure rhinoceros banner had already galloped forth and the long serpent cut itself down; the four quarters were cleared and the eight cords washed clean; your great design was raised afar and benevolent fame carried far; where virtue and transformation reached, the wind blew and grass bent—thus your merit was deeper than slight Yu's and your Way greater than sole Yao's; how could it be only the altars of soil and grain that were settled? The black-haired people likewise relied on you.
translations.idiomatic: You labored at court and sent armies down the rivers; once your forces moved, the rebel host collapsed; you cleared the four quarters and pacified the realm, your design reaching far and your kindness heard abroad; where your rule reached, men yielded like grass in wind—your merit outshone the saviors of old and your Way surpassed the sage kings; it was not only the state that was saved—the people leaned on you.

sentences.zh: 第六皇弟昌，近以妙年出質，提契寇手，偏隔關徼，旋踵末由。

translations.literal: The sixth imperial younger brother Chang, recently sent as hostage in his prime years, fell into the enemy's grasp, cut off beyond the frontier passes, unable to return in a turn of the heel.
translations.idiomatic: Your sixth brother Chang was sent north as a hostage while still young; he fell into enemy hands and was cut off beyond the passes, unable to come home.

sentences.zh: 陛下天倫之愛既深，克讓之懷常切。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's love within the heavenly bonds is already deep, and your constant thought is yielding virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your love for your kin runs deep, and you have long wished to yield your own desire.

sentences.zh: 伏以大德無私，至公有在，豈得徇匹夫之恆情，忘王業之大計。

translations.literal: We submit that great virtue is without selfishness and supreme fairness is ever present—how can one indulge a common man's constant feelings and forget the royal enterprise's great plan?
translations.idiomatic: Great virtue knows no private favor, and supreme justice must prevail—how can private feeling outweigh the needs of the throne?

sentences.zh: 憲章故實，式遵典禮，欽若姬、漢，建樹賢戚。

translations.literal: Take the old precedents as law, follow the ritual canon in form, emulate Zhou and Han, and establish worthy kin.
translations.idiomatic: Follow ancient precedent, observe the rites, and as Zhou and Han did, enfeoff worthy kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 湘中地維形勝，控帶川阜，扞城之寄，匪親勿居，宜啟服衡疑，兼崇徽飾。

translations.literal: The Xiang region's terrain is strategically vital and commands rivers and hills; the charge of guarding the wall none but kin should hold; he should open his fief at Heng and Yi and likewise receive lofty insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang province is a strategic land of rivers and hills; only a kinsman should hold its defense; let him take Hengyang and receive the honors due a prince.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，以昌為使持節、散騎常侍、都督湘州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、湘州牧，封衡陽郡王，邑五千戶，加給皁輪三望車，後部鼓吹一部，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: We your servants jointly propose that Chang be made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in Xiangzhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Xiangzhou; that he be enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang commandery with a fief of five thousand households; and that there be added a black-wheeled carriage with three canopy poles, a rear guard of drums and pipes, and twenty halberd-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that Chang be made bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of armies in Xiangzhou, general of agile cavalry, and governor of Xiangzhou; that he be enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang with five thousand households; and that he receive a black carriage with triple canopy, a guard of drums and pipes, and twenty halberd escorts.

sentences.zh: 啟可奉行。

translations.literal: The memorial may be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Let this memorial be carried out.

sentences.zh: 詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 三月入境，詔令主書舍人緣道迎接。

translations.literal: In the third month he entered the realm; an edict ordered Secretariat clerks to welcome him along the route.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he crossed the border; the throne ordered secretariat clerks to meet him all along the road.

sentences.zh: 景子，濟江，於中流船壞，以溺薨。

translations.literal: On jingzi day he crossed the river; midstream his boat broke and he died by drowning.
translations.idiomatic: On jingzi day he crossed the Yangzi; midstream the boat broke up and he drowned.

sentences.zh: 四月庚寅，喪柩至京師，上親出臨哭。

translations.literal: On gengyin day of the fourth month the bier reached the capital; the emperor went out in person to mourn and weep.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day in the fourth month the coffin reached the capital; the emperor went out in person to mourn.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「夫寵章所以嘉德，禮數所以崇親，乃歷代之通規，固前王之令典。

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued: "Favor and insignia are meant to honor virtue, and ritual is meant to exalt kin—these are the constant rules of successive ages and the fixed statutes of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Honors reward virtue, and ritual exalts kin—this has been the rule of every age and the law of former kings.

sentences.zh: 新除使持節、散騎常侍、都督湘州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、湘州牧衡陽王昌，明哲在躬，珪璋早秀，孝敬內湛，聰睿外宣。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in Xiangzhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Xiangzhou, Prince of Hengyang Chen Chang, had wisdom present in his person and jade and regalia early in bloom; filial reverence steeped within, keen insight shown without.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chang, newly made bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of armies in Xiangzhou, general of agile cavalry, and governor of Xiangzhou, Prince of Hengyang, was wise in himself and gifted from youth, inwardly filial and outwardly sharp.

sentences.zh: 梁季艱虞，宗社顛墜，西京淪覆，陷身關隴。

translations.literal: In Liang's years of hardship the altars toppled; the western capital was lost and he was trapped in the passes of Guan and Long.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's troubled years the dynasty fell; the western capital was lost and he was held captive in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 及鼎業初基，外蕃逆命，聘問斯阻，音介莫通，睠彼機橋，將鄰烏白。

translations.literal: When the great enterprise was first founded, outer regions defied the mandate; envoys were blocked and messages could not pass; we looked on that distant bridge, nearly bordering the crows of dusk.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen house first rose, the frontiers were closed to us; no envoy could reach him and no word come through; we thought of him far away, almost beyond return.

sentences.zh: 今者群公戮力，多難廓清，輕傳入郛，無勞假道。

translations.literal: Now the ministers have joined their strength and many hardships are cleared; light carriages enter the walls without need to borrow a road.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the ministers have joined their strength and the realm is pacified, he could come home without asking leave of any foe.

sentences.zh: 周朝敦其繼好，驂駕歸來，欣此朝聞，庶歡昏定。

translations.literal: The Zhou court honored renewed kinship and the paired horses returned; we rejoice at this morning's news and hope for the evening's comfort of his presence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou once welcomed a kinsman home from captivity; we rejoiced to hear he was coming and hoped at last to see him again.

sentences.zh: 報施徒語，曾莫輔仁，人之云亡，殄悴斯在，奄焉薨殞，倍增傷悼。

translations.literal: Repayment of kindness was only words—he never aided our virtue; when a man is gone, the wasting grief is here; suddenly he died and our mourning redoubled.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven repaid him only with words, not with years; now he is gone and our grief is doubled.

sentences.zh: 津門之慟空在，恆岫之切不追，靜言念之，心焉如割。

translations.literal: The grief at the ford gate is empty; the longing for Mount Heng cannot be pursued; speaking of it in silence, the heart is as if cut apart.
translations.idiomatic: We grieve at the river where he died, but cannot follow him to his grave; to think of it is to feel the heart torn.

sentences.zh: 宜隆懋典，以協徽猷。

translations.literal: Grand honors should be raised to match his bright merit.
translations.idiomatic: Let great honors be granted to match his worth.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、太宰、揚州牧。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, given the yellow battle-axe, made Area Commander over All Military Affairs within and without, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously appoint him palace attendant, grant the yellow battle-axe, make him commander of all armies at court and in the field, grand tutor, and governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 給東園溫明祕器，九旒鑾輅，黃屋左纛，武賁班劍百人，[2]轀輬車，前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: Grant the warm-bright secret vessels of the Eastern Garden, the nine tassels and imperial carriage, the yellow canopy and left banner, a hundred tiger-guard halberd-bearers, [2] the encoffining carriage, and front and rear guards with feather fans, drums, and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Grant the Eastern Garden burial regalia, the nine-tasseled carriage and imperial equipage, a hundred halberd guards, [2] the funeral carriage, and front and rear guards with drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 葬送之儀，一依漢東平憲王、齊豫章文獻王故事。

translations.literal: The rites of burial and escort shall wholly follow the precedents of the Han Prince Xian of Dongping and the Qi Prince Wen of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Burial and escort shall follow the precedents of the Han Prince Xian of Dongping and the Qi Prince Wen of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 仍遣大司空持節迎護喪事，大鴻臚副其羽衛，殯送所須，隨由備辦。

translations.literal: Still dispatch the Grand Minister of Works, bearer of the staff, to meet and escort the funeral; the Grand Herald shall assist with the guard of feathers; whatever the bier and escort require shall be fully provided along the way.
translations.idiomatic: Send the grand minister of works with the staff to receive the coffin; let the grand herald assist with the guard; provide everything needed for the funeral along the route.

sentences.zh: 」諡曰獻。

translations.literal: " Posthumous title: Xian.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Xian.

sentences.zh: 無子，世祖以第七皇子伯信為嗣。

translations.literal: He had no sons; Emperor Wen made his seventh son Boxin heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons; Emperor Wen made his seventh son Boxin his heir.

sentences.zh: 南康愍王曇朗

translations.literal: Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang
translations.idiomatic: Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang

sentences.zh: 南康愍王曇朗，高祖母弟忠壯王休先之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, younger brother of the Founder's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tanlang, Prince Min of Nankang, was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 休先少倜儻有大志，梁簡文之在東宮，深被知遇。

translations.literal: Xiuxian in youth was bold and free with great ambition; when Emperor Jianwen of Liang was in the eastern palace he was deeply favored.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuxian was daring and ambitious in youth; when Emperor Jianwen of Liang was crown prince he won deep favor.

sentences.zh: 太清中既納侯景，有事北方，乃使休先召募得千餘人，授文德主帥，頃之卒。

translations.literal: In Taqing, after welcoming Hou Jing, with affairs in the north he had Xiuxian recruit over a thousand men and appointed him Commander of Wende; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taqing era, after Hou Jing was admitted and war moved north, he had Xiuxian raise more than a thousand men and made him commander of Wende; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 高祖之有天下也，每稱休先曰：「此弟若存，河洛不足定也。

translations.literal: When the Founder had the realm, he often said of Xiuxian: "If this younger brother had lived, settling the Yellow and Luo would not have been hard.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Founder held the realm, he often said of Xiuxian: "If this brother had lived, the Yellow and Luo would not have been hard to recover.

sentences.zh: 」梁敬帝即位，追贈侍中、使持節、驃騎將軍、南徐州刺史，封武康縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Jing of Liang took the throne, he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of South Xuzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Jing of Liang came to the throne, Xiuxian was posthumously made palace attendant, bearer of the staff, general of agile cavalry, and inspector of South Xuzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，追贈侍中、車騎大將軍、司徒，封南康郡王，邑二千戶，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: When the Founder accepted the abdication, he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang commandery with two thousand households, posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, he was posthumously made palace attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and grand tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang with two thousand households, and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 二年，徐嗣徽、任約引齊寇攻逼京邑，尋而請和，求高祖子姪為質。

translations.literal: In year two, Xu Siwei and Ren Yue led Qi invaders to press the capital; they soon sued for peace and asked for the Founder's sons and nephews as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, Xu Siwei and Ren Yue brought Qi armies against the capital; they then sought peace and demanded the Founder's sons and nephews as hostages.

sentences.zh: 時四方州郡並多未賓，京都虛弱，糧運不斷，在朝文武咸願與齊和親，高祖難之，而重違眾議，乃言於朝曰：「孤謬輔王室，而使蠻夷猾夏，不能戡殄，何所逃責。

translations.literal: At the time many commanderies and districts had not yet submitted, the capital was weak, and grain transport was cut off; civil and military officials at court all wished to make peace with Qi, and the Founder found it hard—but he also could not lightly go against the assembly; he then spoke in court, saying: "I wrongly aided the royal house and let barbarians run riot in Xia, unable to destroy them—where can I escape blame?
translations.idiomatic: Many provinces had not yet submitted, the capital was weak, and supplies were failing; court officials all favored peace with Qi, and the Founder was torn—but he could not easily defy them. He told the assembly: "I have poorly served the dynasty and let barbarians ravage the realm without destroying them—how can I escape blame?

sentences.zh: 今在位諸賢，且欲息肩偃武，與齊和好，以靜邊疆，若違眾議，必謂孤惜子姪，今決遣曇朗，棄之寇庭。

translations.literal: Now the worthies in office wish to rest shoulders and lay down arms, make peace with Qi, and quiet the frontier; if I go against the assembly, they will surely say I spare my sons and nephews—today I resolve to send Tanlang and abandon him in the enemy court.
translations.idiomatic: You wish to rest and make peace with Qi to quiet the borders; if I refuse, you will say I spare my kin—today I will send Tanlang and abandon him to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 且齊人無信，窺窬不已，謂我浸弱，必當背盟。

translations.literal: Moreover the Qi are faithless and their coveting does not cease; seeing us weaken day by day, they will surely break the pact.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi are faithless and will not stop their scheming; seeing us weaken, they will surely break the treaty.

sentences.zh: 齊寇若來，諸君須為孤力鬥也。

translations.literal: If Qi invaders come, you gentlemen must fight hard for me."
translations.idiomatic: If the Qi attack again, you must fight for me with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 」高祖慮曇朗憚行，或奔竄東道，乃自率步騎往京口迎之，以曇朗還京師，仍使為質於齊。

translations.literal: The Founder feared Tanlang would dread the journey or flee east along the road; he himself led foot and horse to Jingkou to meet him, brought Tanlang back to the capital, and then sent him as hostage to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder feared Tanlang would refuse or flee east; he went in person with troops to Jingkou to fetch him, brought him back to the capital, and then sent him to Qi as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 齊果背約，復遣蕭軌等隨嗣徽渡江，高祖與戰，大破之，虜蕭軌、東方老等。

translations.literal: Qi indeed broke the pact and again sent Xiao Gui and others to follow Siwei across the river; the Founder fought them and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Qi broke the treaty and sent Xiao Gui and others with Siwei across the Yangzi; the Founder defeated them heavily and took Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others prisoner.

sentences.zh: 齊人請割地并入馬牛以贖之，高祖不許。

translations.literal: The Qi asked to cede territory and present horses and cattle to ransom them; the Founder would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Qi offered to cede land and send horses and cattle as ransom; the Founder refused.

sentences.zh: 及軌等誅，齊人亦害曇朗于晉陽，時〔年〕二十八。

translations.literal: When Gui and the others were executed, the Qi also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; at the time [year] twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui and the rest were put to death, the northerners also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; he was twenty-eight. (The text supplies the missing word "year".)

sentences.zh: [3]是時既與齊絕，弗之知也。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. At the time, already broken with Qi, they did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 3. The court had already broken with Qi and did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，猶以曇朗襲封南康郡王，奉忠壯王祀，禮秩一同皇子。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, he still had Tanlang succeed as Prince of Nankang commandery to maintain the sacrifices to Prince Zhongzhuang, his ritual rank the same as an imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder became emperor, he still had Tanlang recorded as Prince of Nankang to maintain Prince Zhongzhuang's sacrifices, with honors equal to an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，齊人結好，方始知之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiankang, when Qi made peace, they first learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year two, when peace was made with Qi, the court first learned he was dead.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔曰：「夫追遠慎終，抑聞前誥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen issued an edict: "To honor the distant dead and be careful in the final rites—this we have heard in former instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen issued an edict: "To honor the dead and observe the last rites is an ancient teaching.

sentences.zh: 南康王曇朗，明哲懋親，蕃維是屬，入質北齊，用紓時難。

translations.literal: Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, wise and bright in his kinship, was the pillar of the frontier screens; he went as hostage to Northern Qi to ease the time's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang was a worthy kinsman and a pillar of the realm; he went as hostage to Northern Qi to ease the crisis.

sentences.zh: 皇運兆興，未獲旋反，永言跂予，日夜不忘。

translations.literal: The imperial fortune was just rising and he did not yet return; we long looked for him day and night without forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty was rising and he had not returned; we longed for him day and night.

sentences.zh: 齊使始至，凶問奄及，追懷痛悼，兼倍常情，宜隆寵數，以光恆序。

translations.literal: When Qi's envoys first arrived, the grievous news came suddenly; in recalling him our grief doubled beyond the common measure; grand favor should be raised to brighten the constant order.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi's envoys first came, word of his death arrived; our grief was beyond measure; let honors be raised to mark his place.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、安東將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐州刺史，諡曰愍。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of South Xuzhou; posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously appoint him palace attendant, general who pacifies the east, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of South Xuzhou; posthumous title Min.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣兼郎中令隨聘使江德藻、劉師知迎曇朗喪柩，以三年春至都。

translations.literal: " Then he dispatched the acting director of the palace secretariat, together with the envoys on the mission, Jiang Dezao and Liu Shizhi, to meet Tanlang's bier; in spring of year three it reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent the acting director of the palace secretariat, Jiang Dezao and Liu Shizhi, with the embassy to bring Tanlang's coffin home; it reached the capital in spring of year three.

sentences.zh: 初，曇朗未質於齊，生子方泰、方慶。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Tanlang was hostage in Qi, he had sons Fangtai and Fangqing.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tanlang went to Qi as a hostage, he had sons Fangtai and Fangqing.

sentences.zh: 及將適齊，以二妾自隨，在北又生兩子：方華、方曠，亦同得還。

translations.literal: When he was about to go to Qi, he took two concubines with him; in the north he also had two more sons—Fanghua and Fangkuang—who likewise returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent to Qi he took two concubines; in the north he fathered two more sons, Fanghua and Fangkuang, who also came back.

sentences.zh: 子方泰

translations.literal: His son Fangtai
translations.idiomatic: His son Fangtai

sentences.zh: 方泰少麤獷，與諸惡少年群聚，遊逸無度，世祖以南康王故，特寬貰之。

translations.literal: Fangtai in youth was rough and reckless; he gathered with wicked young men and roamed without limit; because of the Prince of Nankang, Emperor Wen especially indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtai was coarse and unruly from youth, running with bad company and living without restraint; because of his grandfather the prince, Emperor Wen especially spared him.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，詔曰：「南康王曇朗，出隔齊庭，反身莫測，國廟方修，奠饗須主，可以長男方泰為南康世子，嗣南康王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, cut off in the Qi court, his return uncertain; the state temple is being restored and sacrifices need a master—his eldest son Fangtai may be made Heir of Nankang and succeed the Prince of Nankang."
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year one an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang is held in Qi and cannot return; the ancestral temple is being restored and needs a master—let his eldest son Fangtai be heir of Nankang and succeed the title."

sentences.zh: 」後聞曇朗薨，於是襲爵南康嗣王。

translations.literal: Later they heard Tanlang had died; thereupon he succeeded to the title of Prince of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Tanlang had died, Fangtai succeeded as Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 尋為仁威將軍、丹陽尹，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General of Benevolent Might and Administrator of Danyang, with staff officers appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general of benevolent might and administrator of Danyang, with a full staff.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，遷使持節、都督廣衡交越成定明新合羅德宜黃利安建石崖十九州諸軍事、[4]平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff and Area Commander over Military Affairs in the nineteen provinces of Guang, Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Ming, Xin, He, Luo, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Jian, Shiya, and others, [4] General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year four he was made bearer of the staff and commander of armies in nineteen southern provinces including Guang, Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Ming, Xin, He, Luo, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Jian, and Shiya, [4] general who pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政殘暴，為有司所奏，免官。

translations.literal: His government was cruel and violent; the responsible offices memorialized against him and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with cruelty; the authorities reported him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋起為仁威將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was reappointed General of Benevolent Might, with staff officers appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as general of benevolent might with a staff.

sentences.zh: 六年，授持節、都督豫章郡諸軍事、豫章內史。

translations.literal: In year six he was given the staff and made Area Commander over Military Affairs in Yuzhang commandery and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he received the staff and was made commander of armies in Yuzhang and interior magistrate of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 在郡不修民事，秩滿之際，屢放部曲為劫，又縱火延燒邑居，因行暴掠，驅錄富人，徵求財賄。

translations.literal: In the commandery he did not attend to the people's affairs; as his term neared its end he repeatedly sent his retainers out to rob, and also set fires that spread through the towns, then went about violent plunder, seizing and registering the rich and extorting wealth.
translations.idiomatic: In office he neglected the people; as his term ended he sent retainers to rob, set fires that burned towns, and plundered openly, seizing the wealthy and extorting bribes.

sentences.zh: 代至，又淹留不還。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived, he still detained himself and would not return.
translations.idiomatic: When his successor arrived he lingered and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 至都，詔以為宗正卿，將軍、佐史如故。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, an edict made him Director of the Imperial Clan, his general's title and staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital an edict made him director of the imperial clan, keeping his general's rank and staff.

sentences.zh: 未拜，為御史中丞宗元饒所劾，免官，以王還第。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he was impeached by the censor-in-chief Zong Yuanrao, removed from office, and sent to his princely residence as a prince only.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office the censor-in-chief Zong Yuanrao impeached him; he was dismissed and sent back to his princely residence.

sentences.zh: 十一年，起為寧遠將軍，直殿省。

translations.literal: In year eleven he was reappointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and assigned to the Direct Palace Office.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he was made general who pacifies the distance and posted to the Direct Palace Office.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍，量置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, with staff appointed as needed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made regular attendant of the Secretariat, with staff as required.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，高宗幸大壯觀，因大閱武，命都督任忠領步騎十萬，陳於玄武湖，都督陳景領樓艦五百，出于瓜步江，高宗登玄武門觀，[5]宴群臣以觀之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year Emperor Xuan visited the Great Zhuang Hall and there held a great review of troops, ordering Area Commander Ren Zhong to lead one hundred thousand foot and horse arrayed at Xuanwu Lake, and Area Commander Chen Jing to lead five hundred tower ships out on the Guazhou stretch of the Yangzi; Emperor Xuan ascended the Xuanwu Gate tower [5] and feasted the ministers to watch.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month Emperor Xuan went to the Great Zhuang Hall for a grand military review, ordered Ren Zhong to array one hundred thousand foot and horse at Xuanwu Lake, and Chen Jing to lead five hundred tower ships onto the Yangzi at Guazhou; Emperor Xuan mounted the Xuanwu Gate tower [5] and feasted his ministers as they watched.

sentences.zh: 因幸樂遊苑，設絲竹會。

translations.literal: He then visited the Leyou Garden and set a music gathering.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the Leyou Garden for a concert.

sentences.zh: 仍重幸大壯觀，集眾軍振旅而還。

translations.literal: He again visited the Great Zhuang Hall, gathered the armies, and returned after displaying their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Great Zhuang Hall, mustered the troops, and marched back in review.

sentences.zh: 是時方泰當從，啟稱所生母疾，不行，因與亡命楊鍾期等二十人，微服往民閒，淫人妻，為州所錄。

translations.literal: At that time Fangtai should have attended; he memorialized that his birth mother was ill and did not go; instead he went with twenty outlaws such as Yang Zhongqi in plain dress among the people and violated men's wives, and was arrested by the province.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtai should have attended but pleaded his mother's illness; instead he went with twenty desperadoes including Yang Zhongqi in disguise among the people and raped women, and was seized by the provincial authorities.

sentences.zh: 又率人仗抗拒，傷禁司，為有司所奏。

translations.literal: He also led men with weapons to resist, wounding the guards, and the responsible offices memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: He also led armed men to resist and wounded the guards; the authorities reported him.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，下方泰獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent Fangtai to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had Fangtai thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 方泰初但承行淫，不承拒格禁司，上曰不承則上測，方泰乃投列承引。

translations.literal: Fangtai at first confessed only to the licentious conduct and did not confess to resisting the guards; the emperor said that if he did not confess they would use torture, and Fangtai then threw himself on the roster and confessed fully.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fangtai admitted only the sexual crimes, not resisting the guards; the emperor said refusal would bring torture, and Fangtai then confessed everything on the record.

sentences.zh: 於是兼御史中丞徐君敷奏曰：[6]「臣聞王者之心，匪漏網而私物，至治之本，無屈法而申慈。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 6. Thereupon the acting censor-in-chief Xu Junfu memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that the heart of a king does not let the net leak to favor things, and the root of supreme order does not bend the law to extend kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 6. The acting censor-in-chief Xu Junfu then memorialized: "I have heard that a ruler's heart does not let offenders slip through the net for private favor, and that supreme order does not bend the law to show mercy.

sentences.zh: 謹案南康王陳方泰宗屬雖遠，幸託葭莩，刺舉莫成，共治罕績。

translations.literal: We respectfully report that Chen Fangtai of the house of Chen, though distant in the clan, has the fortune of kinship by marriage; in impeachment he has no achievement, and in joint governance he has scarce merit.
translations.idiomatic: We report that Chen Fangtai, though a distant kinsman, enjoys the tie of marriage kin; as an inspector he has done nothing, and in office he has achieved little.

sentences.zh: 聖上弘以悔往，許其錄用，宮闈寄切，宿衛是尸。

translations.literal: The sage ruler, in great mercy, allowed him to repent the past and permitted his employment; the palace gates entrusted him with urgent duty, and he was charged with guarding the night watch.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty in mercy let him repent and employed him again; the palace trusted him with urgent duty and made him hold the night watch.

sentences.zh: 豈有金門旦啟，玉輿曉蹕，百司馳騖，千隊騰驤，憚此翼從之勞，妄興晨昏之請？

translations.literal: How could there be, when the golden gate opens at dawn and the jade carriage sets out at daybreak, a hundred offices racing and a thousand squadrons galloping—yet he fears the toil of this winged escort and recklessly raises a morning-and-evening plea?
translations.idiomatic: When the palace gates open at dawn and the imperial carriage sets out, with a hundred offices rushing and a thousand guards riding, how could he shirk escort duty and falsely plead illness morning and night?

sentences.zh: 飜以危冠淇上，袨服桑中，臣子之諐，莫斯為大，宜從霜簡，允寘

translations.literal: Instead he turned his splendid cap toward the Qi River and his bright robes toward the mulberry grove—the fault of a subject, none greater than this; he ought follow the frost record and be permitted placement
translations.idiomatic: Instead he wore fine dress on the streets and took his pleasures in secret—the offense of a subject could hardly be greater; he should be judged by the harsh statutes and be properly

translations.literal: (winter)
translations.idiomatic: (winter)

sentences.zh: 〔秋〕官。

translations.literal: [autumn] office.
translations.idiomatic: [autumn] office.

sentences.zh: [7]臣等參議，請依見事，解方泰所居官，下宗正削爵土。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 7. We your ministers jointly recommend that, according to the present case, Fangtai be removed from the posts he holds and that the Director of the Imperial Clan be ordered to strip his nobility and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 7. We jointly recommend that, on the facts before us, Fangtai be dismissed from office and the Director of the Imperial Clan be ordered to strip his title and fief.

sentences.zh: 謹以白簡奏聞。

translations.literal: Respectfully we report on white tablets.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully submit this memorial.

sentences.zh: 」上可其奏。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋復本官爵。

translations.literal: Soon his former offices and title were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his offices and title were restored.

sentences.zh: 禎明初，遷侍中，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenming era he was made attendant-in-ordinary, keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，隋師濟江，方泰與忠武將軍南豫州刺史樊猛、左衛將軍蔣元遜領水軍於白下，往來斷遏江路。

translations.literal: In year three, Sui forces crossed the Yangzi; Fangtai, together with Fan Meng, General of Loyal Martial Might and Inspector of South Yuzhou, and Jiang Yuansun, General of the Left Guard, led the navy at Baixia to move back and forth cutting off the river route.
translations.idiomatic: In year three the Sui army crossed the Yangzi; Fangtai joined Fan Meng, loyal-martial general and inspector of South Yuzhou, and Jiang Yuansun of the Left Guard in leading a fleet at Baixia to block the river line.

sentences.zh: 隋遣行軍元帥、長史高熲領船艦泝流當之，猛及元遜並降，方泰所部將士離散，乃棄船走。

translations.literal: Sui sent the campaign marshal and chief clerk Gao Jiong to lead ships upstream against them; Meng and Yuansun both surrendered, Fangtai's officers and soldiers scattered, and he abandoned his ships and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sui sent Gao Jiong with a fleet upstream; Fan and Jiang surrendered, Fangtai's men scattered, and he abandoned his ships and fled.

sentences.zh: 及臺城陷，與後主俱入關。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, he entered the Pass together with the Last Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he was taken to the north with the Last Emperor.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中為掖令。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was Director of the Palace Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye reign he served as director of the palace ladies.

sentences.zh: 子方慶

translations.literal: Son Fangqing
translations.idiomatic: Son Fangqing

sentences.zh: 方慶少清警，涉獵書傳。

translations.literal: Fangqing in youth was clear and alert and widely read books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing as a youth was sharp and well read.

sentences.zh: 及長，有幹略。

translations.literal: When grown, he had capacity and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he showed ability and foresight.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，封臨汝縣侯。

translations.literal: In the Tiankang era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru county.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiankang he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linru.

sentences.zh: 尋為給事中、太子洗馬，權兼宗正卿，直殿省。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Supervising Censor, Tutor to the Crown Prince, acting concurrently as Director of the Imperial Clan, and assigned to the Direct Palace Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made supervising censor and tutor to the crown prince, acting director of the imperial clan, and posted to the Direct Palace Office.

sentences.zh: 太建九年，出為輕車將軍、假節、都督定州諸軍事、定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taijian he went out as General of the Light Chariot, acting bearer of the staff, Area Commander over Military Affairs in Dingzhou, and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year nine he was sent out as general of the light chariot, acting bearer of the staff, commander of armies in Dingzhou, and inspector of the province.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，又為散騎常侍，兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he again became Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned as regular attendant of the Secretariat and again directed the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，進號智武將軍、武州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was advanced in title to General of Intelligent Martial Might and Inspector of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year two he was promoted to general of intelligent martial might and inspector of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，廣州刺史馬靖久居嶺表，大得人心，士馬彊盛，朝廷疑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Jing, Inspector of Guangzhou, had long dwelt south of the ranges, won great favor among the people, and had strong troops and horses; the court was suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jing had long governed Guangzhou in the far south, won the people's loyalty, and commanded a strong force; the court grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 至是以方慶為仁威將軍、廣州刺史，以兵襲靖。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fangqing was made General of Benevolent Might and Inspector of Guangzhou and sent with troops to attack Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing was then made general of benevolent might and inspector of Guangzhou and sent to attack Ma Jing with an army.

sentences.zh: 靖誅，進號宣毅將軍。

translations.literal: When Jing was executed, Fangqing was advanced in title to General Who Proclaims Resolution.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was killed, Fangqing was promoted to general who proclaims resolution.

sentences.zh: 方慶性清謹，甚得民和。

translations.literal: Fangqing's nature was pure and careful, and he won great harmony among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing was upright and cautious and governed with popular support.

sentences.zh: 四年，進號雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: In year four he was advanced in title to General of the Cloud Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was promoted to general of the cloud banner.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，隋師濟江，〔東〕衡州刺史王勇遣高州刺史戴智烈將五百騎迎方慶，[8]欲令承制總督征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, Sui forces crossed the Yangzi; [Eastern] Hengzhou Inspector Wang Yong sent Dai Zhilie, Inspector of Gaozhou, with five hundred cavalry to welcome Fangqing, [8] intending to have him take emergency command as overall commander of the armies for suppression and attack.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year three, as Sui crossed the Yangzi, [Eastern] Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong sent Gaozhou inspector Dai Zhilie with five hundred horsemen to fetch Fangqing, [8] planning to put him at the head of all southern armies.

sentences.zh: 是時隋行軍總管韋洸帥兵度嶺，宣隋文帝敕云：「若嶺南平定，留勇與豐州刺史鄭萬頃且依舊職。

translations.literal: At that time Sui's campaign commander Wei Guang led troops across the ranges and proclaimed an edict of Emperor Wen of Sui, saying: "If Lingnan is pacified, Yong and Zheng Wanqing, Inspector of Fengzhou, are to remain in their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Sui commander Wei Guang then crossed the mountains with an edict from Emperor Wen of Sui: if Lingnan were pacified, Yong and Fengzhou inspector Zheng Wanqing would keep their posts.

sentences.zh: 」方慶聞之，恐勇賣己，乃不從，率兵以拒智烈。

translations.literal: " When Fangqing heard this, he feared Yong would sell him out; he would not obey and led troops to resist Zhilie.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing feared Yong meant to betray him, refused, and marched against Zhilie.

sentences.zh: 智烈與戰，敗之，斬方慶於廣州，虜其妻子。

translations.literal: Zhilie fought him, defeated him, beheaded Fangqing at Guangzhou, and captured his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilie defeated him, killed Fangqing at Guangzhou, and took his family prisoner.

sentences.zh: 王勇，太建中為晉陵太守，在職有能名。

translations.literal: Wang Yong, in the Taijian era was Administrator of Jinling and had a reputation for ability in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong had served as Jinling administrator in the Taijian era and was known as an able official.

sentences.zh: 方慶之襲馬靖也，朝廷以勇為超武將軍、東衡州刺史，領始興內史，以為方慶聲勢。

translations.literal: When Fangqing attacked Ma Jing, the court made Yong Super Martial General, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, and concurrent Interior Magistrate of Shixing, to lend weight to Fangqing's campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangqing moved against Ma Jing, the court made Yong super martial general, inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, and interior magistrate of Shixing to strengthen Fangqing's position.

sentences.zh: 靖誅，以功封龍陽縣子。

translations.literal: When Jing was executed, Yong was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longyang county for merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing's death Yong was enfeoffed as viscount of Longyang for his service.

sentences.zh: 及隋軍臨江，詔授勇使持節、光勝將軍、總督衡廣交桂武等二十四州諸軍事、平越中郎將，仍入援。

translations.literal: When Sui armies reached the Yangzi, an edict appointed Yong Bearer of the Staff, Guang Victorious General, overall commander of military affairs in the twenty-four provinces of Heng, Guang, Jiao, Gui, Wu, and others, and General Who Pacifies the Yue, and he was to enter as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: As Sui reached the river, Yong was made bearer of the staff, guang victorious general, commander of twenty-four southern provinces including Heng and Guang, and general who pacifies the Yue, and ordered north to reinforce the capital.

sentences.zh: 會京城陷、勇因移檄管內，徵兵據守，使其同產弟鄧暠將兵五千，頓于嶺上。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Yong thereupon issued proclamations within his jurisdiction, gathered troops to hold the land, and sent his uterine younger brother Deng Hao to lead five thousand men and encamp on the ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell Yong issued calls to arms, mustered troops to hold Lingnan, and sent his younger brother Deng Hao with five thousand men to camp on the pass.

sentences.zh: 又遣使迎方慶，欲假以為名，而自執兵要。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to welcome Fangqing, wishing to borrow his name while himself holding the military keys.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent for Fangqing, hoping to use his royal name while keeping command himself.

sentences.zh: 及方慶敗績，虜其妻子，收其貲產，分賞將帥。

translations.literal: When Fangqing was defeated, Yong captured his wife and children, seized his property, and divided it among his commanders.
translations.idiomatic: After Fangqing's defeat Yong seized his family and goods and shared the loot among his generals.

sentences.zh: 又令其將王仲宣、曾孝武迎西衡州刺史衡陽王伯信，伯信懼，奔于清遠郡，孝武追殺之。

translations.literal: He also ordered his generals Wang Zhongxuan and Zeng Xiaowu to welcome Prince Boxin of Hengyang, Inspector of Western Hengzhou; Boxin was afraid and fled to Qingyuan commandery, and Xiaowu pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Zhongxuan and Zeng Xiaowu to fetch Prince Boxin of Hengyang, inspector of Western Hengzhou; the prince fled to Qingyuan and Xiaowu ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 是時韋洸兵已上嶺，豐州刺史鄭萬頃據州不受勇召，而高梁女子

translations.literal: At that time Wei Guang's troops had already crossed the ridge; Zheng Wanqing, Inspector of Fengzhou, held the province and did not answer Yong's summons, while the Gaoliang woman
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guang had already crossed the mountains; Fengzhou inspector Zheng Wanqing held his province and ignored Yong's call, while the Gaoliang woman

translations.literal: (Hao)
translations.idiomatic: (Hao)

sentences.zh: 〔洗〕氏舉兵以應隋軍，[9]攻陷傍郡，勇計無所出，乃以其眾降。

translations.literal: [Xi] clan raised troops to respond to the Sui army, [9] attacked and captured neighboring commanderies; Yong had no plan left and thereupon surrendered with his host.
translations.idiomatic: [Xi] raised troops for Sui, [9] overran neighboring districts; with no options left Yong surrendered with his army.

sentences.zh: 行至荊州，道病卒，隋贈大將軍、宋州刺史，歸仁縣公。

translations.literal: En route at Jingzhou he fell ill on the road and died; Sui posthumously made him Grand General, Inspector of Songzhou, and Duke of Guiren county.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road at Jingzhou and died; Sui posthumously made him grand general, Songzhou inspector, and duke of Guiren.

sentences.zh: 鄭萬頃，滎陽人，梁司州刺史紹叔之族子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Wanqing was a man of Xingyang, a clansman of Zheng Shaoshu, Inspector of Sizhou in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wanqing of Xingyang was a kinsman of Liang's Sizhou inspector Zheng Shaoshu.

sentences.zh: 父旻，梁末入魏。

translations.literal: His father Min entered Wei at the end of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Min went over to Northern Wei at the end of Liang.

sentences.zh: 萬頃通達有材幹，周武帝時為司城大夫，出為溫州刺史。

translations.literal: Wanqing was penetrating and capable; under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Metropolitan Construction Officer and went out as Inspector of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqing was talented and capable; under Zhou Emperor Wu he was metropolitan construction officer and later inspector of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 至德中，與司馬消難來奔。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era he came to Chen together with Sima Xiaonan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era he defected to Chen with Sima Xiaonan.

sentences.zh: 尋拜散騎常侍、昭武將軍、豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, General Who Manifests Martiality, and Inspector of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regular attendant, general who manifests martiality, and inspector of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州甚有惠政，吏民表請立碑，詔許焉。

translations.literal: In the province he had very benevolent government; officials and people memorialized requesting a stele, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Fengzhou with real kindness; the people petitioned for a commemorative stele and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，萬頃之在周，深被隋文帝知遇，及隋文踐祚，常思還北。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wanqing was in Zhou, he was deeply favored by Emperor Wen of Sui; when Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he often thought of returning north.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou he had been close to the future Sui founder; once Sui was founded he often wished to return north.

sentences.zh: 及王勇之殺方慶，萬頃乃率州兵拒勇，遣使由間道降于隋軍。

translations.literal: When Yong killed Fangqing, Wanqing thereupon led the provincial troops to resist Yong and sent envoys by a secret route to surrender to the Sui army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong killed Fangqing, Wanqing marched against him and sent envoys by a hidden route to surrender to Sui.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Dignitary of the First Rank; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Sui made him a senior dignitary of the first rank; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：獻、愍二王，聯華霄漢，或壤子之暱，或猶子之寵，而機橋為阻，驂駕無由，有隔於休辰，終之以早世。

translations.literal: The historian says: The two princes Xian and Min, linked in splendor in the heavens—one intimate as an earth-son, one favored as like a son—yet the narrow bridge blocked them and the paired carriage team had no way; separated in a good age, they ended in early death.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Princes Xian and Min shone like stars in the sky—one a true brother's son, one cherished like a son—yet barriers kept them apart and they never came home; cut off in a fortunate age, both died young.

sentences.zh: 悲夫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 寔資邢衛 「寔」北監本、汲本、殿本作「式」。

translations.literal: truly relied on Xing and Wei—on "shi": the Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions read "shi" style/ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On "truly relied on Xing and Wei": the character shi—Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions read shi as ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 武賁班劍百人 「武賁」即「虎賁」，避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Tiger guards with a hundred halberd-bearers—"Tiger guard" is "Tiger Brave," changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On "tiger guards, a hundred halberd-bearers": tiger guard renders huben, taboo-avoiding for Tang.

sentences.zh: 北監本、汲本、殿本並已改為「虎賁」。

translations.literal: The Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions have all already been changed to "Tiger Brave."
translations.idiomatic: Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions already read tiger brave.

sentences.zh: 時〔年〕二十八 據北監本、汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: at the time [aged] twenty-eight—supplied according to the Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "at the time [aged] twenty-eight": supplied from Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.

sentences.zh: 都督廣衡交越成定明新合羅德宜黃利安建石崖十九州諸軍事 按數之祇十八州，疑脫一州，或「九」當作「八」。

translations.literal: Area Commander over Military Affairs in the nineteen provinces of Guang, Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Ming, Xin, He, Luo, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Jian, Shiya, and others—counting them there are only eighteen provinces; it is suspected one province is missing, or "nine" should read "eight."
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteen-province command: the list counts only eighteen; one province may be missing, or nine may be an error for eight.

sentences.zh: 高宗登玄武門觀 「觀」汲本、殿本作「親」，屬下讀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan ascended the Xuanwu Gate tower—"tower" in the Ji and Palace editions reads "in person," belonging to the following clause.
translations.idiomatic: On "Emperor Xuan ascended the Xuanwu Gate tower": Ji and Palace read in person, attaching it to the next phrase.

sentences.zh: 張元濟

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanji

sentences.zh: 〈校勘記〉

translations.literal: 〈Collation notes〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation notes〉

sentences.zh: 云：「作『觀』是。

translations.literal: says: "To read 'tower' is correct.
translations.idiomatic: writes: "Tower is correct.

sentences.zh: 觀者，玄武門上之觀也。

translations.literal: The tower is the tower on the Xuanwu Gate."
translations.idiomatic: It means the viewing tower on Xuanwu Gate."

sentences.zh: 」按北監本作「觀」，百衲本南史亦作「觀」。

translations.literal: According to the Northern Supervisor edition it reads "tower"; the Baibaina edition of the History of the Southern Dynasties also reads "tower."
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Supervisor text reads tower; the Baibaina Southern Dynasties history agrees.

sentences.zh: 於是兼御史中丞徐君敷奏曰 「徐君敷」《南史》作「徐君整」。

translations.literal: Thereupon the acting censor-in-chief Xu Junfu memorialized—"Xu Junfu" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xu Junzheng."
translations.idiomatic: On "acting censor-in-chief Xu Junfu memorialized": the Southern Dynasties history reads Xu Junzheng.

sentences.zh: 允寘

translations.literal: Be permitted placement
translations.idiomatic: Be permitted placement

translations.literal: (winter)
translations.idiomatic: (winter)

sentences.zh: 〔秋〕官 據《元龜》五一九改。

translations.literal: [autumn] office—changed according to the Imperial Mirror 519.
translations.idiomatic: On "[autumn] office": emended per the Imperial Mirror 519.

sentences.zh: 〔東〕衡州刺史王勇遣高州刺史戴智烈將五百騎迎方慶 據《南史》補。

translations.literal: [Eastern] Hengzhou Inspector Wang Yong sent Dai Zhilie, Inspector of Gaozhou, with five hundred cavalry to welcome Fangqing—supplied according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Eastern] Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong sent Gaozhou inspector Dai Zhilie with five hundred cavalry to welcome Fangqing": supplied from the Southern Dynasties history.

sentences.zh: 按下文云「朝廷以勇為超武將軍、東衡州刺史」，明此脫一「東」字。

translations.literal: Comment: below it says "the court made Yong Super Martial General, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou"—clearly one character "Eastern" is missing here.
translations.idiomatic: Below the text calls Yong inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, so dong (eastern) is missing here.

sentences.zh: 而高梁女子

translations.literal: While the Gaoliang woman
translations.idiomatic: While the Gaoliang woman

translations.literal: (Hao)
translations.idiomatic: (Hao)

sentences.zh: 〔洗〕氏舉兵以應隋軍 隋書韋洸傳作「高梁女子洗氏」，《通鑑》隋文帝開皇九年作「高涼郡太夫人洗氏」，「浩」與「洗」形近而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: [Xi] clan raised troops to respond to the Sui army—the Biography of Wei Guang in the Book of Sui reads "the Gaoliang woman Xi clan"; the Comprehensive Mirror, Kaihuang year nine of Emperor Wen of Sui, reads "the Grand Mistress Xi of Gaoliang commandery"; "Hao" and "Xi" are alike in form and corrupt—now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Xi] clan raised troops for Sui": the Book of Sui biography of Wei Guang has Lady Xi of Gaoliang; the Comprehensive Mirror (Kaihuang 9) has Grand Mistress Xi of Gaoliang; hao and xi are graphically similar—emended accordingly.
